narrative: Based on your academic record, the model estimated a 55.2% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. The most influential was your third-year class standing. The next most important factor was your undergraduate GPA. At 3.70, it is well above the average for accepted applicants (3.23), and it worked in your favor, moving the prediction toward passing. Your LSAT score had the third-largest influence. At 37, it was nearly identical to the typical accepted student's score, and it also pushed slightly toward passing. Consider retaking the LSAT, adding academic coursework that strengthens your preparation, or asking the admissions office what evidence could support a future application.
